clue.text: Looking back could be costing a pound

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might be rearranged into something else

parts.note: L stands for a pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: Remembering the past turns out to cost a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges COSTING with A and L into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is wistful longing for the past, so the adjective describes someone looking back fondly.

clue.text: 16 turns, changing direction, which isn't common

indicators.note: one compass direction is swapped for another: west becomes north
turns tells us the entry at 16 is read backwards

parts.note: the answer to 16 across is a joint of the arm

explanation.surface: A cross-reference turns about and changes course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' gives WOBLE from 16's answer; 'changing direction' swaps W (west) for N (north).
explanation.definitionFit: Aristocrats are set apart from commoners, so being high-born means not being common.

clue.text: Bird spotted with a boy

parts.note: spotted means saw, past tense of see
Bill is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher sees a bird while out with a young lad.
explanation.definitionFit: The sawbill is a kind of duck, such as the merganser, with a serrated beak.

clue.text: Drink supplied in plastic container

indicators.note: the word plastic acts as a container holding the answer inside it

explanation.surface: A drink is served in a plastic cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian white wine from Piedmont.

clue.text: Dyke appearing as an old banger?

annotationWithheld.why: Dyke appearing as an old banger? (4): GREG Dyke fits the first reading, but no sense of 'an old banger' giving GREG could be confirmed
annotationWithheld.clue: Dyke appearing as an old banger?

clue.text: River in China can be seen with a tube

definitions.text: can be seen with a tube

indicators.note: in places the river inside the old name for China

parts.note: Cathay is an old poetic name for China
the Oder is a river of central Europe

explanation.surface: A river in China can be viewed through a telescope.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the tube named after it: the stream of electrons shows up on the old television screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathode-ray tube is the old television screen, where the electron stream is seen.

clue.text: Outlawry of US lawyer in Hastings

parts.note: outlawry is a ban, an official prohibition
a DA is a District Attorney, a US prosecutor

explanation.surface: An American attorney is barred from practising in the seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Hastings looks like the English town; it is Hastings Banda, first president of Malawi.
explanation.definitionFit: Hastings Banda led Malawi from independence, so his first name defines his surname here.

clue.text: Copper-coloured container

parts.note: blue is a colour, so coloured is read as blue
a bottle is a container

explanation.surface: Describes a vessel with a reddish-brown metal colour.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper-coloured reads as a hue; split it: 'Copper' is a police officer, 'coloured' gives BLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluebottle is old slang for a police officer, from the blue uniform.

clue.text: Religious establishment gets English lines from stage director

parts.note: Trevor Nunn is a famous British theatre director
RY, railway, gives lines of track

explanation.surface: A convent receives English verse from a theatre director.
explanation.definitionFit: A nunnery is a convent, a house where nuns live under religious vows.

clue.text: Stoppers for 6s?

parts.note: 6 down is slang for police officers, and what they do to suspects is halt them by taking them into custody

explanation.surface: Things that plug bottles of a certain kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stoppers' suggests corks; police are the people who stop criminals.
explanation.definitionFit: Police officers take people into custody, so those who do it are stoppers of crime.

clue.text: Singular example of the filth of old London

definitions.text: Singular example of the filth of old London

parts.words: Singular example of the filth of old London
parts.note: the filth is slang for police; one of London's first professional constables, based at a magistrates' court

explanation.surface: One piece of the grime of historic London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The filth' is British slang for the police, not dirt.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bow Street Runners were London's earliest organised police force, founded by Henry Fielding.

clue.text: Old form of communication on the way out

parts.note: ex means former, old
IT is information technology, a means of communicating

explanation.surface: An old means of contact is being phased out.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit is a way out of a building or room.

clue.text: The last people to utter rubbish

definitions.meaning: a last is a shoemaker's foot-shaped block, so its users are shoe repairers

explanation.surface: Those who would be the very last to speak nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobblers use lasts to shape shoes, and cobblers is British slang for nonsense.

clue.text: Budget sweetener?

parts.note: a Budget sweetener is a tax giveaway; read instead as a sugar named after Chancellor Gordon Brown

explanation.surface: A tax concession in the Chancellor's annual Budget.
explanation.walkthrough: A Budget sweetener is a popular tax cut; Gordon Brown was then the UK Chancellor delivering Budgets.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrefined sugar is a sweetener, and the Chancellor's name makes it a Budget one.

clue.text: Doing without money, in want

indicators.note: in puts the money inside the word for want

parts.note: want means lack, absence
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: Going without cash because you are poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstinence is refraining from something, going without it by choice.

clue.text: It's unusual for all beer to be passable

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters of all beer to are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: It is odd that every beer is merely acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerable means acceptable or bearable, which is what passable means.

clue.text: Minority group

parts.note: read minority as being under legal age, so a group of minors

explanation.surface: A social group outnumbered in society.
explanation.walkthrough: Minority reads as a small group; in law it means being under age.
explanation.definitionFit: Young people aged thirteen to nineteen are still minors, under the age of majority.

clue.text: Herb heard for a spell

indicators.note: heard means the word is said out loud

parts.note: a spell is a period of time

explanation.surface: A herb is overheard casting a spell.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is an aromatic herb used in cooking.

clue.text: Joint causes bowel disorder

indicators.note: disorder signals the letters of bowel are jumbled

explanation.surface: A joint problem leads to a stomach upset.
explanation.definitionFit: The elbow is the joint between upper arm and forearm.

clue.text: Flier gets name taken after drink

indicators.note: taken after puts name after the drink

parts.note: bitter is a British beer

explanation.surface: A pilot gets a reputation after drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British draught beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a wading bird of the heron family, and birds fly.

clue.text: They may be laid by railmen working in backstreet …

indicators.note: in places the rearranged railmen within the reversed street

parts.note: ST, street, read backwards

indicators.note: working suggests the railmen's letters are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: Railway workers lay tracks in a side street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backstreet' is one word read as 'back' plus 'street'; 'working' is the anagram signal, and the reversed abbreviation wraps the shuffled workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tramlines are the rails trams run on, laid along streets.

clue.text: Time to press for return of former Central American politician

indicators.note: for return says the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: age means a period of time
to iron is to press clothes

explanation.surface: It is time to push for a former leader to come back.
explanation.definitionFit: Manuel Noriega was Panama's military ruler until the US invasion of 1989.

clue.text: … as trains served by mechanics

indicators.note: served suggests the letters are dished up in a new order

explanation.surface: Continues the previous clue: trains are staffed by skilled workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Artisans are skilled manual workers; mechanic is an old word for such a craftsman.

clue.text: Confine to bed for plagiarism

explanation.surface: Kept in bed as punishment for copying.
explanation.definitionFit: Crib means to restrict, a child's bed, and copying someone else's work.

clue.text: A bit of beef is found on these cattle

indicators.note: a bit of picks out just the first letter of beef

explanation.surface: Some beef comes from these animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Bison are large wild cattle of North America and Europe.

clue.text: Rider loses heart and bladder

indicators.note: loses heart removes the central letters

parts.note: a cyclist rides a bike

explanation.surface: A cyclist gets disheartened and has a bladder problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses heart' removes CLI from the middle of CYCLIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyst is a sac or bladder-like growth in the body.

clue.text: 40 perches squarely over 10

indicators.note: over in a down clue reads the word upwards

parts.note: a rood is an old land measure of forty square perches

explanation.surface: A measurement is given above a number.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition '10' refers to the answer at 10 across, a way out.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer at 10 across means a way out, and a doorway is one.

clue.text: Measures taken in crisis at Austin?

definitions.text: Measures taken in crisis at Austin?

parts.words: Measures taken in crisis at Austin
parts.note: special government measures in a crisis, read as a crisis for the film spy Austin Powers

explanation.surface: Steps taken in an emergency at a car firm.
explanation.walkthrough: Austin suggests the carmaker or the Texas city; it is Austin Powers, the spoof spy of film.
explanation.definitionFit: Governments take special legal powers when facing a national emergency.

clue.text: European man looks older without one

indicators.note: without removes the letter for one

parts.note: senior means older
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A European man appears older without something.
explanation.definitionFit: Señor is Spanish for a man or Mr, the title of a gentleman in Spain.

clue.text: Host about nine holding unusual treat

indicators.note: holding means one set of letters contains the other
about signals the letters of nine are turned around
unusual signals the letters of treat are jumbled

explanation.surface: A host offers around nine people an unusual treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges NINE to EN...IN, 'holding' TERTA, the anagram of TREAT signalled by 'unusual'.
explanation.definitionFit: To host guests is to receive them and look after them, providing hospitality.
